_comment: Single source of truth for externally-sourced tool versions across the dot repo. Consumers read this instead of hard-coding a version/hash inline: nix overlays via builtins.fromJSON, Docker builds via `jq`-fed --build-arg (see faber-stack / docker-claude). `track`: pinned = exact version+hash, bump deliberately; latest = fetched fresh each build, made safe by `anchor`. `pin_fallback` = known-good version to flip a latest tool to when latest breaks. Only tools whose `consumers` include a given surface are wired there yet; others are data pending wiring.

br.note: sha256 below are the GLIBC release tarballs (nix-overlay consumer, autopatched). The portitor-gate is musl Alpine and consumes only `version`: it runs the sha256-pinned install.sh with --version, which selects the static musl build and checksum-verifies it. Keep sha256 in sync with the glibc release when bumping version.

spex.note: Was a buildGoModule rev pin (pre-release main); v0.1.0 is spexmachina's first tagged release, so the box overlays install the prebuilt signed asset (statically linked Go ELF, no autopatchelf). Bump version + both sha256 from the release manifest.json — and mirror them into BOTH faber overlays (spexmachina/, faber-stack-service/), which hard-code the values rather than reading this file.

portitor.note: Was latest+SSHSIG under the Alpine gate; the nix gate pins it by hash (nix builds can't fetch-latest+verify-sig purely). Bump version + refresh sha256 from the release .sha256 assets to move it. 0.3.0 also publishes a separate portitor-mcp binary; the gate installs only portitor.

nixpkgs.note: fetchTarball hash (base32) for the nix-built gate + egress images. Mirrors the box pin in the faber images.yaml files — keep them in sync (that one is read by faber, not this manifest).
